what: SharkNinja designs and sells household appliances under two brands: Shark for vacuums, hair tools and cleaning, and Ninja for blenders, air fryers, coffee makers and outdoor cooking. It launches new products at an unusually fast pace.
customers: Households worldwide, sold through retailers such as Walmart, Target, Costco and Amazon, and increasingly direct.
money: Shark vacuums, steam mops and cleaning products
Ninja air fryers, blenders and coffee machines
Shark hair tools and personal care
moat: A product development machine that turns out dozens of new models a year at prices below premium rivals, with marketing that creates demand before retailers stock them.
risks: Tariffs on goods made in Asia directly raise its costs
Retailer concentration means a few buyers control much of its sales
opportunities: Revenue grew about 16% last year and about 20% a year over three years
Return on invested capital of 20% with modest debt
International markets outside North America are still a small share of sales
watch: New product launch success and international revenue growth.
